Source feature · not telemetry

Long DNS-shaped metadata at the configured threshold.

DATA EXCHANGE · LOCAL FILES + CONTRACTS

Threat context and SIEM/SOAR boundaries

An offline reader handles a completed local STIX bundle, and a bounded writer exports local SIEM projections. SOAR handoff remains an inert contract. None provides a live feed, cloud sender, credential, scheduler, or response path.

Offline / inert
STIX 2.1Offline threat contextReader implemented

An explicit library call reads one owner-private completed file with an exact digest, 16 MiB / 4,096 object / 32-level / 15-second ceilings.

  • Immutable bounded provenance and markings
  • Patterns remain inert untrusted text
  • No TAXII, persistence, model, attribution, or action
ECS · OCSFLocal SIEM projectionLocal writer implemented

Bounded ECS 9.5.0 and OCSF 1.9.0 profiles can publish a complete new local file without replacing an existing destination.

  • 10,000 records / 16 MiB maximum
  • No payload or event.original
  • No collector, credential, or network delivery
SOARInert handoffZero attempt

A provider-neutral contract can describe review state while remaining incapable of delivery or response.

  • Destination not configured
  • Zero attempts; status not attempted
  • No endpoint, webhook, playbook, or host action

The hosted page cannot open a local bundle. The reader and local writer have source and synthetic-test evidence only; this does not establish threat-intelligence authenticity, SIEM compatibility, delivery, coverage, or production acceptance. Read the exchange boundary ↗

User install · Linux

Install once. Open like an app.

Three steps to a local, read-only workspace. Start from a reviewed checkout. The installer adds MEGALODON for your user only; companion tools and data can come later.

  1. 01

    Review

    Use Python 3.11 or newer on Linux. Download or clone the project, then review the source and local setup guide.

    Open the merged install source on GitHub ↗Local setup guide ↗
  2. 02

    Install

    From the repository root, create the private user application and menu entry:

    ./scripts/install-local.sh

    No sudo. Python may download build requirements. Optional tools, sensors, telemetry, and automatic startup are not installed.

  3. 03

    Open and check

    Open MEGALODON from the application menu, then choose Home → Data and tools → Check this computer.

    Open a running local HUD ↗

    The app opens your browser after its local server binds. On a phone, 127.0.0.1 points to the phone. This Site cannot tell whether your HUD is running.

Prefer to run the checkout without installing?

Use the source launcher from the repository root:

./scripts/start-local.sh

Keep its terminal open and stop with Ctrl+C. The source launcher does not add an app-menu entry or change an existing Python installation.

An empty local HUD means evidence is unavailable, not zero traffic.

Produces

      SAFETY MEMBRANE

      Trust membrane

      Autonomy stops before authority.

      Detections support review; they do not prove malicious activity. Model advice is untrusted commentary, never evidence or permission to change a host.

      Security review ↗
      01

      Metadata only

      No packet payloads or payload-derived hashes enter the core event model.

      02

      Loopback by default

      Core telemetry reads stay on 127.0.0.1:8787. A separate, disabled-by-default AI question POST requires an operator token and writes private AI receipts. This hosted Site cannot call either local route.

      03

      Local core operation

      The local core requires no cloud account. This hosted Site uses hosting/sign-in services; external setup links leave the Site.

      04

      Plan, do not apply

      Firewall proposals are inert. Live application remains explicitly refused.

      05

      Bounded local AI

      The optional client allows one bounded loopback request with no action authority. The separately operated model process is not confined by those client checks.

      06

      Finite evidence

      Implemented operations have documented bounds. The Suricata 512 MiB logical store ceiling is not a whole-disk or retention budget; retention remains operator-owned.

      Evidence flow

      One-way by design

      1. 01Bounded inputJSONL or a supported bounded adapter
      2. 02Fixed detectionSYN flood, port scan, DNS tunneling
      3. 03Atomic evidenceAudit ledger and terminal receipts
      4. 04Read-only reviewLocal dashboard and private reports

      Where the bytes live

      Tracked source vs. runtime-only storage

      Quoted from docs/storage-layout.md ↗. Cloning this repository creates only the left lane; the right lane exists only after an operator runs the named command.

      Tracked in git

      • config/*.tomlTyped defaults and the fixed detection-rule reference
      • contracts/*/v1/Inert schemas and accepted/rejected fixtures
      • megalodon/reference/*Pinned IANA snapshot and synthetic evaluation corpus
      • site/dist/This static console mirror; no process reads it at runtime
      run a command →

      Runtime-only, gitignored

      • data/megalodon.dbAudit ledger; 256 MiB default high-water stop
      • captures/, logs/Operator-authorized adapter input, never created automatically
      • offline-runs/One mode-0700 report-set directory per analysis run
      • --suricata-db <path>Operator-selected store; 512 MiB logical ceiling

      No command shares one path across stores. Each keeps its own owner-private directory and mode checks, so one store's failure or migration cannot touch another's.
